about: Economy rules read by engine.py on every step; edit them and the next turn uses the new values. A copy goes into each turn's manifest. Amounts are per year (one turn), in each product's unit.

food.about: decay is the base share of a tile's holdings lost at the end of each year; economy_modifiers() in engine.py turns it into a per-tile rate, which is where future products and infrastructure will change it. A product that keeps better (preserved food, say) is a separate product with its own rate. Food that isn't eaten is all lost by the next turn.

foraging.about: Hunting and gathering. Labor H (person-hours a year of the activity) yields P = max * (1 - exp(-return_per_hour * H / max)): about return_per_hour per hour while labor is light, levelling off at the tile's sustainable maximum. max = (land area x the cover-weighted yield_per_km2 x landform factor x climate factor + water area x water_yield_per_km2) x river_factor if the tile has a navigable river. Yields come from observed forager densities: about 800,000 kcal per person per year.

climate.about: Land yields fall linearly from full at full_to_latitude degrees north or south to min_factor at min_at_latitude and beyond.
